rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s promise of poverty and command to indecency mean taking something unlawfully and putting it where it does not belong.
rows.anchor: يأخذوا الشيء من غير حله، ويضعوه في غير محله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek God’s face seek His approval and are never absent from Him for an hour.
rows.anchor: يريدون وجه الله ورضاه، ولا يغيبون عنه ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most ascetic people are those whose food is purest.
rows.anchor: أزهد الناس أصفاهم مطعما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most devout people work hardest at keeping God’s commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أعبد الناس أشدهم اجتهادا في القيام بالأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people most beloved to God are most sincere toward His creatures.
rows.anchor: أحبهم إلى الله أنصحهم لخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl defines a wasted lifespan as one that is squandered.
rows.anchor: وسئل عن العمر قال: الذي يضيع العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the verse describes a servant directing every movement and stillness toward God, as in the description of those who respond to their Lord.
rows.anchor: فهو قصد العبد في حركاته وسكونه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Experiencing both the seeking servant and the one sought is a favor from God, who joins them in saying every blessing comes from Him.
rows.anchor: فكل من وجد حال المريد والمراد فهو من فضل الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker exerts intention, worship, and effort to find God’s path and remains in pursuit; the one sought receives God’s enabling, performs obedience without strain, and then rises through higher stations.
rows.anchor: المريد الذي يتكلف القصد إليه والعبادة لله تعالى ويطلب الطريق إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stations are found in the angels’ description: each has a known station.
rows.anchor: هي موجودة في كتاب الله تعالى في قصة الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil comprises disbelief, hypocrisy, and major sins; the good is faith, whose ranks include prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and the righteous.
rows.anchor: الخبيث على ضروب: الكفر والنفاق والكبائر، والطيب على ضروب: وهو الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God piles the evil together in layers according to their sins, as shown by the hypocrites’ lowest level in Hell.
rows.anchor: ثم يجعل الخبيث بعضه على بعض على مقدار ذنوبهم طبقة طبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever seeks worldly status through knowledge receives the reward for the work in this life but nothing in the next, because the work was not sincere for God.
rows.anchor: يعني من أراد بعلمه غير الله آتاه الله أجر عمله في الدنيا، فلا يبقى له في الآخرة شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person knew God had subjected the world and its people to seekers of the afterlife, he would not display his knowledge for show.
rows.anchor: ولو علم أن الله سخر الدنيا وأهلها لطلاب الآخرة لم يراء بعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincerity is the hardest thing for the ego because it has no share in it.
rows.anchor: أي شيء أشد على النفس؟ فقال: الإخلاص.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even faith, the root of religious duties, can be corrupted by showing off and become hypocrisy; deeds are still more vulnerable.
rows.anchor: قد دخل الإيمان الذي هو أصل الفرائض حتى أبطله وصار نفاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A show-off is someone whose outward conduct escapes blame while God knows that the inward state contradicts it.
rows.anchor: فكل من لم يعب أحد عليه في ظاهره، ويعلم الله خلافه من سره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two prisoners were called young men because neither outdid the other in making a claim and each referred matters to his companion.
rows.anchor: ورجعا في كل ما كان لهما إلى صاحبهما، فسماهما فتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel visited Joseph in prison, conveyed God’s rebuke for seeking an intermediary, and foretold years more in prison; when Joseph learned God was pleased with him, he was unconcerned.
rows.anchor: حكي أن جبريل صلوات الله عليه دخل على يوسف في السجن، فقال له جبريل:

rows.speaker: علي ابن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali compared disciplining his own soul to a shepherd who gathers his flock on one side only for it to scatter on another.
rows.anchor: وكان علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه يقول: ما أنا ونفسي إلا كراعي غنم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم والشعبي
rows.claim: Ibrahim and al-Shaʿbi say this verse was abrogated by the verse prohibiting wine.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية نسخت بآية الخمر، كذا قال إبراهيم والشعبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Sahl, intoxication is whatever intoxicates the soul in this world while leaving its consequence in the afterlife uncertain.
rows.anchor: السكر عندي ما يسكر النفس في الدنيا، ولا تؤمن عاقبته في الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة
rows.claim: Abu Hamza lists four intoxications: drink, youth, wealth, and political power.
rows.anchor: أخبرنا أن السكر أربعة. فقال: اعرضها علي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl adds two forms of intoxication: a scholar’s love of worldly life and a worshipper’s desire to be noticed.
rows.anchor: فقال: وسكرتان لم يخبرك بهما. فقال: ما هما؟ فقال: سكر العالم إذا أحب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths’ request for mercy means asking God to preserve them in remembrance of Him.
rows.anchor: أي احفظنا على ذكرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called youths because they believed in God without an intermediary and approached Him after shedding their attachments.
rows.anchor: لأنهم آمنوا به بلا واسطة، وقاموا إليه بإسقاط العلائق عن أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The increase in guidance means increased insight in faith.
rows.anchor: هدى } [13] أي بصيرة في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s leading someone astray means allowing the wretchedness already known of that person to appear by withholding protection; no one can then protect him.
rows.anchor: من يرد الله منه إظهار ما علم منه من الشقاوة بترك العصمة إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog’s outstretched forelegs signify obedience to command and prohibition.
rows.anchor: أي باسط ذراعيه بالأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says al-raqim means an ink pot in the Roman language.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: الرقيم الدواة بلسان الروم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says al-raqim is the valley containing the cave.
rows.anchor: الحسن: الرقيم الوادي الذي فيه الكهف

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says al-raqim is a lead tablet recording the youths’ names, lineages, religion, and origin of flight.
rows.anchor: كعب: الرقيم لوح من رصاص فيه أسماؤهم وأنسابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wasid means the space immediately in front of a door.
rows.anchor: وأما الوصيد فهو فناء الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the youths bodily would make an observer flee, but seeing them through the Real reveals within them the realities of divine unity.
rows.anchor: لوليت منهم فرارا، ولو اطلعت عليهم بالحق لوقفت على حقائق الوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward meaning is political authority; inwardly, it is the spirit, the intellect’s understanding, and the heart’s alertness through remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: ظاهرها الولاية، وباطنها نفس الروح وفهم العقل وفطنة القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness is wasting one’s time in idleness.
rows.anchor: قال: الغفلة إبطال الوقت بالبطالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart has a thousand deaths, culminating in separation from God, and a thousand lives, culminating in meeting the Real.
rows.anchor: إن للقلب ألف موت، آخرها القطيعة عن الله عز وجل، وإن للقلب ألف حياة، آخرها لقاء الحق عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every sin brings death to the heart, and every act of obedience brings it life.
rows.anchor: وإن في كل معصية للقلب موتا، وفي كل طاعة للقلب حياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God willed refers to His pre-eternal knowledge, which no one knows but God.
rows.anchor: ما شاء الله في سابق علمه، لا يقف عليه أحد إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of having no power except through God means people cannot fulfill the original command, remain safe from its consequences, or reach a good end without divine help.
rows.anchor: لا قوة لنا على أداء ما أمرتنا به في الأصل والسلامة منه في الفرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl glosses the prophetic formula as having no escape from ignorance at the root or persistence in its branches except through God’s protection, nor power to obey except through His help.
rows.anchor: لا حول عن السلامة من الجهل في الأصل، ومن الإصرار في الفرع إلا بعصمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best gift to a servant is knowledge that makes him grow in dependence on God.
rows.anchor: ما أفضل ما أعطي العبد؟ قال: علم يستزيد به افتقارا إلى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The love God grants is an unveiling that the innermost secrets receive without an intermediary, a station for those truthful in private and public.
rows.anchor: أي مكاشفة تتخذ الأسرار من غير واسطة. وهذا مقام من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer faces forward and repeatedly charges rather than fleeing, striving through monotheism, following the Prophet, constant supplication, and hope of communion through emulation.
rows.anchor: المؤمن وجه بلا قفا، كرار غير فرار، تراه يجاهد في دين الله وطاعته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Zayd ibn Aslam says everyone in the Prophet’s community enters Paradise except whoever refuses: obedience admits one, while disobedience is refusal.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما من أمتي إلا دخل الجنة إلا من أبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who follows appetite is content when the heart is pleased and the soul enjoys its immediate share; otherwise appetite turns him back toward disbelief.
rows.anchor: يعني الذي يتبع الهوى إن رضي قلبه وفرحت نفسه بعاجل حظها اطمأن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse calls for the patience of people of spiritual knowledge: the messengers before endured contentedly and submissively, without complaint or despair.
rows.anchor: اصبر صبر أهل المعرفة، كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl counts twelve resolute prophets: Abraham accepted fire and the sacrifice of his son; Job endured affliction; Ishmael accepted sacrifice; Noah endured denial; Jonah prayed in the whale; Joseph remained unchanged through well and prison; Jacob lost sight and child but complained only to God.
rows.anchor: الرسل إبراهيم صلوات الله عليه، ابتلي بالنار وذبح الولد فرضي وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is a sleeping soul and the afterlife is an awake soul.
rows.anchor: الدنيا نفس نائمة، والآخرة نفس يقظانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path to salvation begins with knowledge, bears fruit in resisting appetite and avoiding prohibitions, then disciplines the soul to fulfill commands in purity; this makes worship easy and leads to the stations of worshippers and their spiritual tasting.
rows.anchor: أصل ذلك العلم، ثم ثمرته مخالفة الهوى في اجتناب المناهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Abraham, thirsty in a hot desert, asked an Abyssinian herdsman for water; the man struck a rock and water sprang out.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن عليه الصلاة والسلام أصابه يوما عطش شديد

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: God says He would have removed the heavens and earth at the herdsman’s request because the man wanted nothing in either world but God.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس يريد من الدنيا والآخرة غيري

rows.speaker: عامر بن عبد القيس
rows.claim: Amir ibn Abd Qays says he gave up women and collecting water, while accepting sleep and food as unavoidable needs to manage as best he could.
rows.anchor: وقال عامر بن عبد القيس: وجدت الدنيا أربع خصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks a servant about duties owed to the self, to the knowledge between the servant and God, and to the intellect; one should fulfill these through careful attention to the outcome.
rows.anchor: يسأل الله تعالى العبد عن حق نفسه، وحق العلم الذي بينه وبين ربه، وحق العقل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says that at a person’s death other people ask what he left behind, while the angels ask what he sent ahead.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قال: إذا مات ابن آدم قالت بنو آدم: ما ترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children must not distract from performing obligations on time; anyone diverted from God’s remembrance and service by worldly desire and then pleased with worship is deceived, except one God takes.
rows.anchor: عن أداء الفرائض في مواقيتها، فإن من شغله عن ذكر الله وخدمته

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman said he did not weep from fear of death or greed for the world, but because the Prophet had instructed them to keep only a traveler’s provision; his possessions were modest bedding and utensils.
rows.anchor: فقال سلمان: أما إني لست أبكي جزعا على الموت، ولا حرصا على الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s instruction was that one’s worldly provision should be no more than a traveler’s supplies.
rows.anchor: ليكن بلغة أحدكم من الدنيا مثل زاد الراكب

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman advised Saʿd to remember God when he intends, when he judges, and when he swears.
rows.anchor: اذكر الله تعالى عند همك إذا هممت، وعند حكمك إذا حكمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being’s restlessness means fluctuating with the movements of desire and following appetite.
rows.anchor: يعني متقلبا في حركات الشهوات واتباع الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a person becomes poor he grieves, and when he becomes wealthy he withholds.
rows.anchor: إذا افتقر حزن، وإذا أثرى منع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshippers are people of gnosis who recognize the value of things: they rejoice only in God, find rest only in Him, and grieve at separation from Him.
rows.anchor: العارفين بمقادير الأشياء، فلا يكون لهم بغير الله فرح، ولا إلى غيره سكون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report describes the best of the Prophet’s community as people who laugh openly at God’s broad mercy yet weep privately from fear of His punishment, remember and supplicate to Him, long for Him, burden others lightly, and discipline themselves.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " من خيار أمتي فيما نبأني الملأ الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command teaches dependence on and refuge in God, and to express that dependence; this guides believers and further misleads disbelievers. True monotheism attends to, turns toward, and relies on God alone, rejecting all else.
rows.anchor: أمره بالافتقار واللجوء إليه، ثم بإظهارهما بقوله، ليزيد بذلك للكافرين ضلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only prophets and some, not all, of the truthful are free from appetite; freedom requires disciplining the self, and only prophets and some truthful people attain perfect discipline and character.
rows.anchor: لا يسلم من الهوى إلا نبي وبعض الصديقين ليس كلهم، وإنما يسلم من الهوى

rows.speaker: ابن السماك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sammak told his students that the cure they sought was to oppose their desires.
rows.anchor: وخرج ابن السماك يوما إلى أصحابه وقد اجتمعوا إليه فقال لهم: قد كثرت عظاتي لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the final flight, Abel flees Cain, Muhammad flees his uncle, Abraham his father, Lot his wife, and Noah his son.
rows.anchor: هابيل من قابيل، وسيدنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من عمه، وإبراهيم من أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward meaning of dawn is the morning.
rows.anchor: ظاهرها الفجر الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passing night of the gathering takes away what it contains.
rows.anchor: ليلة الجمع تذهب بما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the dawn is Muhammad, from whom the lights of faith, obedience, and both worlds burst forth.
rows.anchor: منه تفجرت أنوار الإيمان وأنوار الطاعات وأنوار الكونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the night is Muhammad’s community, the vast multitude.
rows.anchor: أمته وذلك السواد الأعظم كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that during the Night Journey the Prophet saw a vast multitude between heaven and earth; Gabriel identified them as his community, including seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning, untouched by sins or worldly defilement and knowing only God.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ليلة أسري بي رأيت سوادا عظيما ما بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes being created in hardship to mean being created amid difficulty and distress.
rows.anchor: أي في مشقة وشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl also explains al-kabad as uprightness: the human is created upright in the mother’s womb.
rows.anchor: قال: الكبد الانتصاب، أي لقد خلقناه في بطن أمه منتصبا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the child stands upright in the womb like its mother; an angel raises its head when she lies down, or it would drown in blood.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: إن الولد يكون في بطن أمه منتصبا كانتصاب الأم، وملك موكل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeding in a day of hunger is necessary sustenance for faith, not an indulgence in the injustice and excess of natural appetite.
rows.anchor: ضرورة الإيمان قواما، لا ظلما وطغيانا بلذة نفس الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual counsel in patience means patience in obeying God, while mutual mercy means compassion among creatures.
rows.anchor: يعني بالصبر على أمر الله، والتراحم بين الخلق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked about Islam, the Prophet answered patience and generosity; asked about faith, he answered wholesome speech and feeding people.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما الإسلام؟ فقال: " الصبر والسماح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl says the best speech is remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: سهل: وأطيب الكلام ذكر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is the light of faith: it dispels ignorance’s darkness and extinguishes the flame of Hell.
rows.anchor: نور الإيمان يجلي ظلمة الجهل، ويطفئ لهيب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, night is sin and persistence in sin covering faith’s light so it does not shine in the heart or appear in a person’s qualities.
rows.anchor: يغشى نور الإيمان، فلا يشرق في القلب، ولا يظهر أثره على الصفات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that appetite and desire overcome knowledge and reason.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الهوى والشهوة يغلبان العلم والعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the night signifies the natural self.
rows.anchor: قال: باطنها نفس الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day signifies the spirit.
rows.anchor: والنهار إذا تجلى } [2] نفس الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human endeavors differ: some are sincere and some are mixed with contingencies.
rows.anchor: فمنه ما هو خالص ومنه ما هو مشوب بالأحداث

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr gave his utmost from himself and wealth, avoided settling into the natural self, and affirmed the good promise as the word of monotheism.
rows.anchor: أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أعطى من نفسه وماله مجهوده، واتقى سكونه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed interpretation identifies al-husna with the reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالجزاء

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another unnamed interpretation identifies al-husna with sincerity.
rows.anchor: ويقال: هو الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The easy path is a return to goodness.
rows.anchor: هو العود إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl’s miserliness was withholding obedience to God and His Messenger, while his self-sufficiency was a show of needing neither.
rows.anchor: أبو جهل بخل بطاعته لله ورسوله، واستغنى: أظهر من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the hard path easy by enabling the person to perform the deeds of Hell; his wealth cannot help when he falls into it.
rows.anchor: أي نسهل عليه العمل، بعمل أهل النار، ألا تراه كيف قال عقبه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most Godfearing is the truthful one, identified as Abu Bakr: others gave and feared, but he let go of the perishable and kept the everlasting.
rows.anchor: الأتقى هو الصديق هو أتقى الناس فإن الناس أعطوا واتقوا وهو لم ير الفاني وأبقى لنفسه الباقي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Prophet asked what he had kept for himself, Abu Bakr answered: God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ماذا أبقيت لنفسك؟ قال: الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the morning brightness represents the spirit.
rows.anchor: هو نفس الروح في الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is the natural self becoming calm in the spirit’s company through continual remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: يعني نفس الطبع إذا سكن إلى نفس الروح في إدامة الذكر إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God magnifies hope through grace and hidden gentleness by mentioning ease twice; the Prophet said one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: عظم الله تعالى حال الرجاء في هذه الآية بكرمه وخفي لطفه، فذكر اليسر مرتين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying about one hardship not overcoming two eases is read inwardly as the heart’s insight and intellect overcoming the natural self and returning it to sincerity.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لن يغلب عسر يسرين "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best form means the finest stature and appearance.
rows.anchor: أي في أحسن قامة وأحسن صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being returned to the lowest state means passing from one condition to another until old age.
rows.anchor: يعني نقلناه من حال إلى حال حتى أدركه الهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who did good in youth continue to have the deeds of their youth recorded when weakness and old age prevent them from performing them.
rows.anchor: في شبابهم، فإنهم إذا ضعفوا وشاخوا أمرنا الملائكة تكتب لهم الأعمال التي كانت تكتب لهم حال شبابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward does not cease even when they can no longer perform the deeds.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينقطع عنهم أجور أعمالهم وإن ضعفوا عنها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the oath as invoking the Lord of Time.
rows.anchor: قيل: أي ورب الدهر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes it as the afternoon or time itself.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person in loss is Abu Lahab, who lost all his days.
rows.anchor: يعني أبا لهب خسر أيامه كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿun means household utensils.
rows.anchor: قال: الماعون متاع البيت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says al-maʿun means alms.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿun also means wealth in the language of Abyssinia.
rows.anchor: وهو المال بلغة الحبش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A masculine demonstrative after feminine فتنة is explained by an understood masculine noun: this matter you were hastening.
rows.anchor: فذكر بعد التأنيث كأنه أراد: هذا الأمر الذي كنتم به تستعجلون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In الرفث إلى نسائكم, إلى is used because rafath here has the meaning of ifḍāʾ; normally one says rafatha bi-imraʾatihi.
rows.anchor: قال: إنما دخلت "إلى" لأن معنى "الرفث" و"الإفضاء" واحد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic usage can put bi in place of إلى or على, as in أحسن بي for أحسن إلي, غما بغم for غما على غم, and تأمنه بقنطار for على قنطار.
rows.anchor: وإنما هو "أحسن إلي" فلم "إلى" ووضع "الباء" مكانها

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s علي is used for عني, providing evidence that Arabic prepositions can substitute for one another.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: - وأخبرني من أثق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلوا إلى شياطينهم can be compared with both خلوت إليه and خلوت به; إلى may also mean مع, as in من أنصاري إلى الله, while من can mean على in ونصرناه من القوم.
rows.anchor: وذا يشبه {وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم} لأنك تقول: "خلوت إليه وصنعنا كذا وكذا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يرشدون is from رشد يَرشد; Arabs also use رشد يَرشُد, and the verse has been read يَرشدون.
rows.anchor: لأنها من: "رشد" "يرشد" ولغة للعرب "رشد" "يرشد"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وتدلوا is jussive when coordinated with the preceding prohibition.
rows.anchor: جزم على العطف ونصب اذا جعله جوابا بالواو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, وتدلوا is accusative as the consequence expressed by the coordinating waw.
rows.anchor: ونصب إذا جعله جوابا بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحج is genitive because it is coordinated with الناس.
rows.anchor: فجر {الحج} لأنه عطفه على "الناس" فانجر باللام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولكن البر من اتقى means the righteousness of whoever is Godfearing.
rows.anchor: وقال {ولكن البر من اتقى} يريد "بر من اتقى".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فبهت الذي كفر, Abraham stunned the disbeliever; the form بهت is better and more common.
rows.anchor: أي: بهته إبراهيم و {بهت} أجود وأكثر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أو كالذي مر على قرية, the comparative كاف is extra, linking the example back to the challenge about Abraham; likewise ليس كمثله شيء means ليس كهو, since God has no likeness.
rows.anchor: الكاف زائدة والمعنى - والله اعلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ in لم يتسنه may be a pause marker and then drop in connected speech, like اخشه; some retain it in connection as original, which is the reading Akhfash follows.
rows.anchor: فتثبت الهاء للسكوت واذا وصلت حذفتها مثل {إخشه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word سنة may derive from waw or hāʾ; Arabic forms such as سنية, سنيهة, أسنتوا, مساناة, and مسانهة preserve the competing derivations.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يجعلها من الهاء فيقول: "سنيهة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhfash relates ننشزها to نشر, opposite of folding; others use ننشرها to mean raise, supported by نشز هذا and أنشزته.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم {ننشرها} أي: نرفعها. تقول: "نشز هذا" و"أنشزته".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indicative أعلم means I know when the speaker refers to himself; the jussive اعلم is an imperative to another, or self-admonition, and is semantically better but less often read. Akhfash follows the common nominative reading.
rows.anchor: إذا عنى نفسه. وقال بعضهم {قال اعلم} جزم على الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s request to see how God revives the dead expresses neither doubt nor a request for inner vision; he wanted to see with his eyes.
rows.anchor: فلم يكن ذلك شكا منه ولم يرد. به رؤية القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s question أولم تؤمن means Have you not already believed? A poet’s ألستم خير من ركب المطايا similarly expects an affirmative answer.
rows.anchor: يقول: "ألست قد صدقت" أي: أنت كذاك.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s line ألستم خير من ركب المطايا illustrates the rhetorical question as an assertion of what is already true.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: [من الوافر وهو الشاهد الثالث والثلاثون] :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms بربوة and برباوة are all Arabic dialects for a high place, from الرابية and the verb ربا يربو.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم {بربوة} و {بربوة} و {برباوة} و {برباوة} كل من لغات العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أكل names food, while الأكل can name the act of eating; the poem’s أَكلة and جوعة show the action reading, though aḍḍamma can mean a portion of food.
rows.anchor: و"الأكل" هو الفعل الذي يكون منك. تقول: "أكلت أكلا"

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s أَكلة, with fatḥa, means an act of eating, as reinforced by جوعة in the same line.
rows.anchor: قال: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد الثامن والأربعون بعد المئة] :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وابل is heavy rain; Arabic uses both وبَلت and أوبلت as it uses مطرت and أمطرت, and parallel paired forms for dew and rain. The earth is موبولة, while أخذا وبيلا means severe.
rows.anchor: وتقول في "الوابل" وهو: المطر الشديد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذرية ضعفاء and the other form ذرية ضعافا are equivalent plural forms; فعيل can take plurals like ظراف and ظرفاء.
rows.anchor: وكل سواء لأنك تقول: "ظريف" و"ظراف" و"ظرفاء"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some compare الفقر with the two forms of الضعف and analyze يعد as taking two objects.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم {الفقر} مثل: "الضعف" و"الضعف" وجعل "يعد" متعديا الى مفعولين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine pronoun in فإن الله يعلمه can follow the latter item, the vow; similar masculine reference can summarize giving and concealment or refer to the meaning of an action.
rows.anchor: تحمل الكلام على الآخر كما قال {ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نذر ينذر names making a vow; one also says نذرت مالي, as Akhfash reports from Yunus and illustrates with Mary’s vow.
rows.anchor: وقوله {أو نذرتم} تقول: "نذر" "ينذر على نفسه" "نذرا"

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses ينذرون and أنذر in an oath involving the speaker’s blood, attesting the verb for making a vow.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: [من مجزوء الكامل وهو الشاهد التاسع والأربعون بعد المئة]

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antarah’s الناذرين illustrates the same vow usage, pledging blood if the speaker does not meet them.
rows.anchor: وقال عنترة*: [من الكامل وهو الشاهد الخمسون بعد المئة]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes فتطردهم an accusative consequence of the statement that neither party is accountable for the other.
rows.anchor: فالأولى أن ينصب جوابا لقوله {ما عليك من حسابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, فتطردهم is linked as an accusative consequence to the prohibition ولا تطرد, followed by فتكون من الظالمين.
rows.anchor: والأخرى [أن] ينصب بقوله {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة أنه من عمل, أنه substitutes for الرحمة and explains that God decreed that whoever acts thus will receive mercy.
rows.anchor: فقوله {أنه} بدل من قوله {الرحمة} أي: كتب أنه من عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فأنه clause begins a new sentence meaning that forgiveness and mercy belong to the repentant person; some instead treat فأن as a noun with its predicate omitted.
rows.anchor: وقوله {فأنه} على الابتداء أي: فله المفغرة والرحمة فهو غفور رحيم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some analyze فأنه as a noun with an unexpressed predicate, effectively stopping at فأن.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم {فأنه} أراد به الاسم وأضمر الخبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أن in وما لهم ألا يعذبهم الله is extra, though it still has grammatical effect; a poetic line is cited for an extra particle.
rows.anchor: ف {أن} ها هنا زائدة - والله أعلم - وقد عملت

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The line لو لم تكن غطفان لا ذنوب لها supplies poetic evidence for an extra particle, using لا in the construction.
rows.anchor: قال: [من البسيط وهو الشاهد السابع والأربعون بعد المئة]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مكاء وتصدية is accusative as the predicate of كان.
rows.anchor: عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية} نصب على خبر "كان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ليميز may come from doubled ميز; some lighten it as يميز from ماز يميز, which is the reading Akhfash adopts.
rows.anchor: جعله من "ميز" مثقلة وخففها بعضهم فقال {ليميز} من "ماز" "يميز"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At a pause, ملجأ has no final alif because it has no tanwīn; by contrast, a pause on the tanwīn accusative ملجأً retains alif.
rows.anchor: عليها ولا تقول (ملجأ ا) لانه ليس ها هنا نون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading وليجدوا فيكم غلظة is the one Akhfash adopts; غلظة is another dialect form.
rows.anchor: وبها نقرأ وقال بعضهم (غلظة) وهما لغتان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا, أي is nominative as the subject after the verb’s effect falls on the feminine pronoun; it needs no preceding verb because it itself supplies the question.
rows.anchor: ف"أي" مرفوع بالابتداء لسقوط الفعل على الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative أيكم is also possible by analogy with the reported accusative construction زيدا ضربته.
rows.anchor: ومن نصب "زيدا ضربته" في الخبر نصب "أي" ها هنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متاع الحياة الدنيا means this is the provision of worldly life; the fuller sense is متاعكم متاع الحياة الدنيا.
rows.anchor: أي: وذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا. وأراد "متاعكم متاع الحياة الدنيا".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كماء means like the likeness of water, with مثل understood.
rows.anchor: يريد: كمثل ماء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وازينت represents وتزينت: tāʾ assimilates into the nearby zāy, then a connecting alif is added because the word cannot begin with a still consonant; the heavy form reflects the same source.
rows.anchor: يريد "وتزينت" ولكن أدغم التاء في الزاي لقرب المخرجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كان is jussive in the conditional, with نوف as its response.
rows.anchor: ف (كان) في موضع جزم وجوابها (نوف)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة is parsed as a predicate of a definite noun.
rows.anchor: وقال {ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة} على خبر المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مرية may be read with either kasra or ḍamma; both are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقال {فلا تك في مرية منه} وقال بعضهم (مرية) تكسر وتضم وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ويتلوه شاهد منه has an unexpressed predicate.
rows.anchor: وقال {أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ويتلوه شاهد منه} وأضمر الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فالنار موعده calls the Fire itself the appointment, though the destination is in it, as Arabic idiom can say the moon is tonight; the cited verse likewise says their appointment is morning.
rows.anchor: وقال {فالنار موعده} فجعل النار هي الموعد وإنما الموعد فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سآوي is treated as a first-person form IV verb, explaining the word’s hamza and its reference to the speaker.
rows.anchor: ف"أنا أغيضه" وتقول: "غاضته الأرحام" ف"هي تغيضه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا عاصم may mean there is no protector; alternatively it means no possessor of protection, with من رحم as a nominative substitute for العاصم.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على "لاذا عصمة" أي: معصوم ويكون (إلا من رحم) رفعا بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غاض can be transitive as in غِضته أغيضه and intransitive as in غاضته الأرحام تغيضه, paralleling وما تغيض الأرحام.
rows.anchor: ف"أنا أغيضه" وتقول: "غاضته الأرحام" ف"هي تغيضه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nisba yāʾ in الجودي is doubled, as if the mountain were attributed to al-jūd, like البصري and الكوفي.
rows.anchor: وأما (الجودي) فثقل لأنها ياء النسبة فكأنه أضيف الى "الجود"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تطغوا comes from طغوت تطغا, like محوت تمحا.
rows.anchor: وقال {ولا تطغوا} من "طغوت" "تطغا" مثل "محوت" "تمحا".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تركنوا is from ركن يركن; another vocalization is also possible from the same verb.
rows.anchor: وقال {ولا تركنوا} لأنها من "ركن" "يركن" وان شئت قلت "ولا تركنوا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ in طرفي النهار is vocalized because it meets a following still consonant; still consonants are usually given kasra, as in صاحبي السجن.
rows.anchor: وقال {طرفي النهار} فحرك الياء لأنها ساكنة لقيها حرف ساكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زلفا is a plural of زلفة, with زلفات and زلف also used as plural forms.
rows.anchor: وقال {وزلفا من الليل} لأنها جماعة تقول "زلفة" و"زلفات" و"زلف"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وكلا نقص عليك, كلا is the object of نقص; the following ما clause says what strengthens the Prophet’s heart.
rows.anchor: وقال {وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل} على "نقص" {ما نثبت به فؤادك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين, one bāʾ connects the verb to its object, while the other is licensed by the negation ما.
rows.anchor: فاحدى الباءين أوصل بها الفعل الى الاسم والاخرى دخلت ل"ما" وهي الاخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وادكر is form VIII from ذكرت, underlyingly اذتكر; adjacent sounds assimilate, but dāl preserves voicing instead of ta, and ṭāʾ is avoided because it is emphatic.
rows.anchor: وانما هي "افتعل" من "ذكرت" فأصلها "اذتكر"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say مذكر, replacing tāʾ with dhāl before assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم (مذكر) فابدل التاء ذالا ثم ادخل الذال فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reading أن يصلحا, ṣād does not assimilate into tāʾ because of voicing and emphasis; tāʾ becomes ṣād instead, while يصطلحا is the better form.
rows.anchor: فابدلوا التاء صادا وقال بعضهم (يصطلحا) وهي الجيدة.

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: Some scholars say all the women tried to seduce Joseph, rather than only the ruler’s wife.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم: "انهن راودنه لا امرأة الملك"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address راودتن can be used even of one woman, just as الناس can refer to one man in the report about Abu Sufyan.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز وإن كانت واحدة أن تقول "راودتن"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of أيقاظ is يقظ; the plural of يقظان is يقاظ.
rows.anchor: وقال {أيقاظا} واحدهم "اليقظ"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فلينظر does not govern أيها directly because النظر can be followed by a question, as in انظر أزيد أكرم أم عمرو.
rows.anchor: تقول: "انظر أزيد أكرم أم عمرو".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما يعلمهم إلا قليل means only a few people know their number; the noun people is understood.
rows.anchor: أي: ما يعلمهم من الناس إلا قليل. والقليل يعلمونهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا أن يشاء الله means unless you say إن شاء الله; in a long statement, an indication of this kind suffices because one part points to the whole.
rows.anchor: أي: إلا أن تقول: "إن شاء الله" فأجزأ من ذلك هذا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سنين may be a substitute for ثلاث or for مئة; it is genitive if it explains مئة and accusative if it explains ثلاث.
rows.anchor: على البدل من {ثلاث} ومن "المئة" أي: لبثوا ثلاث مئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبصر به وأسمع is an exclamation meaning How perceptive and hearing He is!, like أكرم به; a command would instead be أكرمي زيدا.
rows.anchor: أي: ما أبصره وأسمعه كما تقول: "أكرم به" أي: ما أكرمه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تعد عيناك uses the dual sense: your two eyes should not turn away from them.
rows.anchor: وقال {ولا تعد عيناك عنهم} أي: العينان فلا تعدوان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقل الحق من ربكم means Say: it is the truth from your Lord, with هو understood.
rows.anchor: وقال {وقل الحق من ربكم} أي: قل هو الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وساءت مرتفقا means the abode is a bad resting place.
rows.anchor: وقوله {وساءت مرتفقا} أي: وساءت الدار مرتفقا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although أجر من أحسن عملا is grammatically singular, it refers to the plural believers and therefore means their rewards.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما قال {لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا} كان في معنى: لا نضيع أجورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بلاغ means: that is a communication or message.
rows.anchor: يقول: ذاك بلاغ.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say al-balagh is the Quran, since admonition is delivered through the Quran; the following بلاغ then restates that point.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "إن البلاغ هو القرآن" وإنما يوعظ بالقرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألفافا has the singular form لف.
rows.anchor: وواحدها "اللف".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جزاء وفاقا means a recompense corresponding to their deeds, with a verbal noun pattern like قاتل قتالا.
rows.anchor: يقول "وافق أهمالهم وفاقا" كما تقول: "قاتل قتالا".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كذابا is a verbal noun shaped to match the quadriliteral pattern of أفعلت إفعالا; Arab usage also has قاتل قيتالا.
rows.anchor: لأن فعله على أربعة أراد أن يجعله مثل باب "أفعلت" "إفعالا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كل is accusative by attraction to the preceding accusative; although the verb is occupied by its pronoun object, an implicit verb also governs كل.
rows.anchor: فنصب {كل} وقد شغل الفعل بالهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم ينظر المرء ما قدمت يداه can mean he looks at what his hands sent ahead, with ما modified by قدمت.
rows.anchor: فان شئت جلعت: "ينظر أي شيء قدمت يداه"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some instead understand ينظر إلى ما قدمت يداه, with إلى omitted.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "إنما هو" ينظر الى ما قدمت يداه فحذف "الى".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw in وما خلق الذكر والأنثى coordinates the day oath with the earlier oath.
rows.anchor: فهذه الواو واو عطف عطف بها على الواو التي في القسم الأول.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the oath to invoke the Creator of male and female, with وما خلق الذكر والأنثى explaining or substituting for ما.
rows.anchor: فجعل القسم بالخلق كأنه أقسم بما خلق ثم فسره
